# Role Data Schema

The TypeScript interface for each role in the `gameRoles` array. Every role must have all required fields. Optional fields are marked.

```typescript
interface GameRole {
  // Identity
  title: string;              // Official role name (e.g., "Season Facilitator")
  emoji: string;              // Single emoji representing the role
  characterName: string;      // Archetype name (e.g., "The Gardener")
  tagline: string;            // One-line summary, 3-7 words (e.g., "Keeps the seasons turning")

  // Images (generated by nano-banana-pro)
  characterImage: string;     // Path to card portrait: "/images/roles/[slug]-card.webp"
  sceneImage: string;         // Path to full scene: "/images/roles/[slug]-scene.webp"

  // Sociocratic structure
  purpose: string;            // 1-2 sentences. What this role exists to do. Written directly to the person who'd fill it.
  circle: string;             // Which circle this role belongs to
  powers: string[];           // 3-5 items. What this person CAN DO that others can't.
  rights: string[];           // 3-4 items. What access/authority this role carries.
  responsibilities: string[]; // 3-5 items. What this person commits to delivering.
  domains: string;            // Comma-separated areas this role owns.

  // Compensation
  band: number;               // 1-7, maps to the band table below
  tokenAward: string;         // Human-readable base compensation (e.g., "700,000 $ReGen ($7,000)")
  maxTokenAward: string;      // With full Seed+Harvest bonus (e.g., "910,000 $ReGen ($9,100)")
  hoursPerWeek: number;       // Expected hours per week commitment
  deliverables: string[];     // 3-5 items. What compensation is tied to. These are the outputs.

  // Seed and Harvest (bonus system)
  seed: string;               // The planting commitment: did you do the work? Deliverable-based.
  harvest: string;            // The ecosystem impact: did it grow? Outcome-based, measured at Season Festival.

  // Timing and status
  seasons: string[];          // Which seasons this role is most active: ["winter", "spring", "summer", "fall"]
  assignment: string;         // Current status: "Open", "Filled", "Partially filled", "Golden opportunity", etc.
  color: string;              // Hex color for card accent

  // Optional
  specialContent?: {
    title: string;
    body: string;
    coworkLink?: string;
    coworkCta?: string;
    prompt?: string;
  };
}
```

## Compensation Bands

7 bands with a 3:1 ratio (highest to lowest). Steps of 100,000 $ReGen between each band.

| Band | $ReGen/Season | USD Value | Bonus at +30% | USD w/ Bonus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 900,000 | $9,000 | 1,170,000 | $11,700 |
| 6 | 800,000 | $8,000 | 1,040,000 | $10,400 |
| 5 | 700,000 | $7,000 | 910,000 | $9,100 |
| 4 | 600,000 | $6,000 | 780,000 | $7,800 |
| 3 | 500,000 | $5,000 | 650,000 | $6,500 |
| 2 | 400,000 | $4,000 | 520,000 | $5,200 |
| 1 | 300,000 | $3,000 | 390,000 | $3,900 |

**$ReGen value:** $0.01 per token (benchmark set Season 1).

**Bonus logic:**
- Seed planted AND harvest comes in = +30% of base
- Only one (seed or harvest) = +15% of base
- Neither = base only

## Seed and Harvest Model

Every role has two accountability metrics, framed as a natural cycle:

**Seed** = the planting commitment. Did you do the work you said you'd do? This is deliverable-based and mostly binary. Either you shipped it or you didn't. Examples: "sessions held," "content published," "reviews completed."

**Harvest** = the ecosystem impact. Did other people benefit from your work? This is outcome-based and measured at the Season Festival by looking at what actually happened in the community. Examples: "new members who came back," "players completing quests," "contributors who merged their first PR."

The framing matters. These are not KPIs. They're a way of asking: did you plant, and did the garden grow? Some harvests take longer than a season. Partial credit exists for a reason.

**What makes a good Seed metric:**
- Clearly within the role holder's control
- Observable by the community (not hidden in a dashboard)
- Binary or close to it (did you do the thing?)

**What makes a good Harvest metric:**
- Measures benefit to other people, not efficiency of the role holder
- Naturally visible in the community
- Doesn't incentivize gaming (measuring "responses received" not "emails sent")
- Can be tracked from existing systems (forum DB, GitHub, signup tracking, Season Festival survey)

## Circles

| Circle | Domain |
|---|---|
| Anchor Circle | Core governance, game design |
| Incubation Circle | Season facilitation, project support |
| Alliance Circle | Partnerships, investor relations |
| Projects Circle | Land project guidance, mentoring |
| Community Circle | Forum, tools, quests, community health |
| Communications Circle | Content, outreach, storytelling |
| Finance Circle | Treasury, budgets, financial reporting |
| Tech Circle | Code, security, skills, infrastructure |

## Seasons Array Schema

```typescript
interface Season {
  name: string;
  emoji: string;
  months: string;
  theme: string;
  description: string;
  activeRoles: string[];  // Must match gameRoles titles exactly
  color: string;
  current: boolean;
}
```

## Naming Conventions

**Character names** follow "The [Noun]" pattern. Warm, specific, archetypal. Good: "The Gardener", "The Tinkerer", "The Cartographer". Avoid: "The Leader", "The Helper", "The Worker".

**Taglines** are 3-7 words, present tense. Poetic but concrete. Good: "Keeps the seasons turning", "Maps the paths players walk". Avoid: "Makes things happen", "Helps the team".

**Image slugs** from role title, lowercase, hyphenated: "season-facilitator", "grand-builder".

## Color Guidelines

- `#7dd87d` -- Living green (growth, community roles)
- `#fbbf24` -- Golden amber (opportunity, design/tech roles)
- `#4a9f4a` -- Deep forest green (stewardship, guidance roles)
- `#d4a574` -- Warm wood/copper (outreach, alliance roles)
- `#93c5fd` -- Cool blue (winter/building roles, used sparingly)

No reds, no alarm colors. Everything inviting.

## Season Festival Scorecard

At the end of each season, every role holder fills out a scorecard:

| Question | Scale | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| Was the scope right? | 1-5 | Role definition quality |
| Was the compensation fair? | 1-5 | Band accuracy |
| Did you have what you needed? | 1-5 | Support and tooling |
| One thing to change: | Free text | Specific improvement |

This data goes into `seasons/season-N-name.md` and feeds the cross-season tracking table in `SEASONS_HISTORY.md`.
